Title: AKU Trains 61 Community Savings Leaders
NewsSummary: Training boosts Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA) leaders in financial management
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan University (AKU) Arusha Campus recently concluded a highly successful two-day leadership training, significantly strengthening community-based savings groups operating under the Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA) methodology. Held in November, at the AKU Community Outreach Centre, the programme brought together 61 dedicated participants, surpassing the original target of 60, including nine Village Agents and 52 Group Leaders.

This initiative is a critical step towards enhancing local financial inclusion and resilience. Facilitated by Ms. Eda Dyausa (AKU-FSA), Sosthenes Milobo (AKU- Community Engagement and Training Officer), and District Community Development Officer Josephine Mshana, the sessions provided practical, hands-on training. Key topics covered Community-Based Savings Group (CBSG) leadership structures, effective meeting procedures, proper share-out processes, and the crucial step of online group registration, aligning groups with government regulations.

The engagement and impact were notable. Attendance reached an impressive 101.67%, with participants actively contributing to discussions and exercises. Furthermore, the knowledge transfer was profound: pre- and post-training evaluations showed a significant leap in understanding, with average scores climbing from 51.9% to 69.3%.

While minor logistical challenges related to time management were noted due to participants' agro-pastoral responsibilities, facilitators quickly proposed flexible scheduling and streamlined content delivery as solutions.

The training concluded on a wave of optimism, with leaders committing to strengthening record-keeping, formalizing their groups through online registration, and establishing sustainable payment agreements for Village Agents. As one facilitator noted, "This training marks a turning point for community savings groups. It's about empowering leaders to drive financial inclusion and resilience."
